I have 2 switches (layer 3), in a branch office. One is a the edge, routing back to a main office and the other is Access for the hosts. I have a number of VLANs I want to configure.

Am I correct with the following:

  • I should configure the VLANs on both switches, but with different SVI's eg Switch A: 192.168.1.254/24. Switch B: 192.168.1.253/24?

  • Both the interfaces interconnecting the two switches should be configured with dot1q encapsulation?

  • For ospf to route the traffic back to the main office I need to configure it on the Edge switch for all VLANS as well as the network that will carry the traffic? On the Main office switch I need to configure it just for the traffic network.

  • I DO NOT need to configure sub-interfaces on either switch because they are layer 3?

Are there any other things I should be aware of?

Do any the interconnecting interfaces need to be configured with IP addresses?

Thanks very much! :)

Generally speaking and with a number of assumptions... :

  1. You only need SVIs for every VLAN if you're using a FHRP or each switch is going to have a different IP subnet for the same VLAN (IE routed access design) Otherwise on the other switch you just need a management SVI somewhere.
  2. Both switch uplinks will be configured with dot1q if you want each VLAN to span both switches. As above if each VLAN will be a different IP subnet on each switch, you'd probably make that a routed interface or part of a L3 port channel.
  3. To advertise routes to the new subnets your network command or ospf commands on the interfaces will need to cover all of those subnets or at least be redistributing a route that covers those subnets. You will have to have a network command that covers the subnet that connects to the remote site.
  4. Correct, you do not need to configure sub-interfaces on either switch.

Now that I've answered your questions directly here's what I'd do to get it done and off my plate (This assumes a few things about your network that i can't know for sure from your post)

  1. Sounds like this is a small branch office so skip routed access and just let the core switch do inter-vlan routing
  2. Layer 2 etherchannel between the two switches
  3. Management SVI somewhere on second switch
  4. Network statement to cover all attached interfaces IE: router ospf 1 network 0.0.0.0 255.255.255.255 area X passive default no passive-interface (whatever your L3 uplink to other branch is) (whatever additional authentication options you may have)

  5. On main site router enable OSPF for uplink to new site router ospf 1 network x.x.x.x 0.0.0.0 area x (covering new interface) no passive-interface (L3 uplink to new site)

  6. management, individual port configs, company policy, best practices, etc for both switches.

If you have additional detail or questions throw em up here!
